rules.summary: The cap on critic rounds per feature (in EVO, per increment), counting every review path.
searches: grep -rniE 'rounds?|cap' <paths>: read each hit about critic or review rounds

rules.summary: The default review level (R1 for SDD and EVO) and Critical features always at R2.
searches: grep -rniE 'critical[^.]*(R2|review)|default[^.]*R1|review level' <paths>

rules.summary: What each review level runs (R0 no critic, R1 one critic, R2 the cycle) and which levels have a critic. Naming the levels (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; what a level runs is always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rnE '\bR[012]\b' <paths>: read each hit that says what a level runs

rules.summary: Review level with the depth gate off or under a standing acceptance: a raise applies and is reported, a lowering is asked; a standing acceptance covers only the default.
fingerprints: \blevel you recommend and the programmer validates\b
searches: grep -rniE 'raise|lower|standing acceptance' <paths>: read each hit about the review level

rules.summary: DIRECT runs a clean critic only when the programmer asks for one.
searches: grep -rniE 'DIRECT[^.]*(critic|review)' <paths>

rules.summary: As executor at R1, a second critic on the fixes runs only if the programmer asks.
searches: grep -rniE 'critic on the fix' <paths>

rules.summary: A later critic round reports only Blocker and Major findings in the diff since the previous round.
searches: grep -rniE 'only (the )?Blocker' <paths>

rules.summary: Hard stops stop the feature in every gate profile.
searches: grep -rniE 'hard stop|every (gate )?profile|any profile' <paths>: read each hit that says what stops regardless of the profile

rules.summary: Which events are hard stops: a mention outside the source names one only with a pointer to protocols/gates.md §Hard stops (or the bare protocols/gates.md, or §Hard stops) in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters before or after it.
searches: grep -rniE 'hard stop|stops? (the feature )?(always|regardless|whatever)' <paths>: read each hit that names an event as a hard stop

rules.summary: When the critic-round cap is reached with a Blocker or Major finding of any round still open, the feature stops and asks the programmer. What counts as open is always a copy outside the source; naming the stop (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not.
searches: grep -rniE 'cap|rounds? run out|(blocker|major)[^.]*open' <paths>: read each hit about what happens when the critic rounds end with findings open

rules.summary: Commits made after the last critic round (its fixes included) are listed with their hashes as unreviewed before acceptance, never presented as reviewed. Naming them as unreviewed (names) next to a pointer to the source, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \bthe fixes of (?:that|the last|the final) round included\b
searches: grep -rniE 'unreviewed|not (been )?reviewed|after the last (critic )?round' <paths>: read each hit about commits that no critic saw

rules.summary: In auto, a decision that chooses which of two or more rules the author wrote prevails stops the feature and goes to the programmer; what counts as a rule the author wrote (not the behavior of code). Naming it (names) next to a pointer to protocols/gates.md §When a gate is off, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
rules.pointer: protocols/gates\.md ?§ ?when a gate is off|§ ?when a gate is off
searches: grep -rniE 'rules? (the author|you) wrote|written by the author|authored rule|contradict[^.]*rules?|decided by agent' <paths>: read each hit about who settles a choice between written rules in auto

rules.summary: When an agent is resumed and when a relay replaces it: the per-model token caps, the 100k band, what a point follow-up is, and the usage thresholds read from subagent_tokens. Naming the cap (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 Reusing agents, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; a number or a threshold is always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rniE 'resum|relay|replac|subagent_tokens|[0-9]+ ?k\b|follow-up' <paths>: read each hit that says when an agent is resumed or replaced

rules.summary: The relay: the outgoing agent is resumed for one turn to write relay notes (exploration only, no diffs, contents or logs) under the git common dir; the orchestrator writes them when it cannot; the new agent reads the notes and the full diff. Naming the relay notes or their folder (names) next to a pointer to protocols/context-handoff.md §Relay, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'relay|one turn|notes' <paths>: read each hit about how a same-role replacement starts

rules.summary: Pause versus stop everything: on a pause running agents finish and no new delegation starts; on stop everything they are stopped at once and their IDs recorded; the resume state lists finished, interrupted and to-relaunch work, and interrupted work is relaunched, never assumed done. Naming stop everything (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §7, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'paus|stop (everything|all)|running agents|interrupted|relaunch' <paths>: read each hit about what happens to running agents when work stops

rules.summary: In auto, a catch-up in the SKILL.md §5 shape goes to the programmer unasked at each phase or increment transition; the move into acceptance counts, the start of the feature does not; the auto increment report takes that shape. Naming the catch-up next to a pointer to SKILL.md §5, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \bstart of the feature (?:does not|doesn't|adds no|is not)\b
searches: grep -rniE 'catch-up|transition|increment report|as a report' <paths>: read each hit about what the programmer is told unasked in auto

rules.summary: The first reach mapping of a broad statement searches by concept (meaning, synonyms, paraphrases, restatements, places that apply the rule without naming it), every search is recorded, and a place found late is recorded as a discovery with the search that found it. Naming the concept search (names) next to a pointer to knowledge/edge-cases.md §Before code, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'by concept|synonym|paraphras|restatement|search(es)? (run|recorded)|found so far' <paths>: read each hit about how the reach of a broad statement is searched

rules.summary: When a decision or statement that cases depend on changes during an increment, the Test Designer is resumed or relayed at once, before the Tester's next run, to retire or update every dependent case; with no dependent case it is not resumed; each case records what it depends on. Naming it (names) next to a pointer to roles/test-designer.md §Decisions that cases depend on, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \bnever runs? a case that asserts a superseded\b
searches: grep -rniE 'depend(s|ent)? on|superseded|retire' <paths>: read each hit about what happens to cases when a decision changes

rules.summary: Cases that check text artifacts assert the presence and meaning of what the source requires, not its exact wording, so a rewording that keeps the rule does not fail them. Naming it (names) next to a pointer to roles/test-designer.md §Cases that check text, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'wording|brittle|rewording|text (check|artifact)|presence and meaning' <paths>: read each hit about how tests check prose

rules.summary: Every copy of a touched rule is searched across skills/, README.md and docs/ and fixed in the same round; verification commands (copy checker, unit tests, quality gate) run after committing, on a clean tree, as separate steps. Naming it (names) next to a pointer to roles/implementer.md §Rules touched and verification, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
fingerprints: \btests? compare the base commit with the committed head\b
searches: grep -rniE 'all copies|every copy|copies of|clean tree|after committing|same round' <paths>: read each hit about copies of a touched rule and when verification runs

rules.summary: Who writes tests: the Test Designer derives the cases, the Tester implements and runs them, the Implementer writes production code only; the exceptions (a fixture or helper the plan assigns, the check or test of an approved anti-pattern entry, DIRECT). Naming the division (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 Who writes tests, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; the exceptions and who derives or implements the cases are always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rniE 'writes? (no |its |the )?tests?|code and tests|production code only|fixture or helper|never writes' <paths>: read each hit about who writes tests and the exceptions

rules.summary: Model floors: no haiku for the specification, planning, test design, the critic, the verifier, a specialist audit or a phase runner; Critical features use opus for them. Naming a floor (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 Model selection per delegation, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; which roles and which Critical upgrades are always a copy outside the source.
fingerprints: \bhaiku\b[^.;]{0,40}\b(?:must not|should not|not be used|is not allowed|forbidden|banned)\b
searches: grep -rniE 'haiku|floors?|opus if critical' <paths>: read each hit about a model floor or the Critical upgrade

rules.summary: The standard model and agent type of each role and the typical deviations (down to haiku, up to opus). Naming a role's model next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 is not a copy; a table of roles with their models or a deviation condition is always a copy outside the source.
searches: grep -rniE '(general-purpose|Explore|Plan)[` ]*· ?(opus|sonnet|haiku)|haiku if|opus if' <paths>: read each hit that gives a role's standard model or a deviation

rules.summary: What each gate profile (full, key, auto) does with each gate: which gates stop, which are off and what the agent does in their place. Outside the source a profile may be named, and chosen with --gates, but never described gate by gate.
searches: grep -rniE '`?(full|key|auto)`?[^.]{0,40}(stops|every gate|only at)|gate profiles?|`?(defects|discoveries|depth|increment)`?( gate)? (is |are )?off' <paths>: read each hit that says what a profile does with a gate

rules.summary: When handoff.md is written: at a phase transition, only when the incoming agent is new, in orchestrator mode only (a new agent of a role that already ran gets relay notes; a resumed agent gets a brief). Naming the handoff for a new agent (names) next to a pointer to protocols/context-handoff.md, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; the condition is always a copy outside the source.
fingerprints: \bonly when a new agent takes over\b
searches: grep -rniE 'handoff[^.]{0,60}new agent|incoming agent is new|only when the incoming|no handoff' <paths>: read each hit about when a handoff is written

rules.summary: When state.md is written: at every stop (a gate, a pending question, the end of the turn, a pause or a stop everything), by whoever drives the session; the card's State plays it in EVO as executor. Naming it (names) next to a pointer to protocols/context-handoff.md §Resume state, in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy; the list of stops is always a copy outside the source.
fingerprints: \ba gate, a pending question,? (?:and )?the end of the turn\b
searches: grep -rniE 'every stop|at a stop|a pending question, the end of the turn|resume state' <paths>: read each hit about when state.md is written

rules.summary: Parallel launches: independent tasks run in parallel within a feature and across features; within one feature never two code-modifying agents at the same time. Naming the parallel launch (names) next to a pointer to SKILL.md §4 Delegation practice (Grouping), in the same paragraph, cell or list item and within 60 characters, is not a copy.
searches: grep -rniE 'in parallel|code-modifying|at the same time|at once' <paths>: read each hit that states a general rule of launching agents in parallel
